title: Influencers Cause Tennis Etiquette Debate at US Open
paragraphs: Tennis has long been known for its strict etiquette. Spectators are expected to stay quiet during points and to avoid moving around while players are serving. However, at this year's US Open in New York, a group of social media influencers sparked a heated debate about how fans should behave at tennis matches.

The controversy began during a first-round match between Naomi Osaka and Anastasia Zakharova at Arthur Ashe Stadium. A group of influencers who were filming a TikTok video in a luxury suite made so much noise in the middle of a point that play had to be briefly stopped. A video of the incident, which showed the group shouting a line together while people seated nearby looked annoyed, quickly went viral. The chair umpire paused the match and asked the group to be quiet. Danny Singer, who recorded the video, called it one of the cringiest things he had ever seen live.
There were also reports of influencers using bright ring lights during points and standing in areas where they were not allowed.

Several players spoke out. Osaka called on spectators to respect tennis etiquette. Jessica Pegula said she appreciated influencers showing people the US Open experience, but added that filming with lights during play was disrespectful to players. Coco Gauff said she welcomed new fans but hoped they would respect the traditions of the sport.

The tournament had invited nearly 100 content creators in 2026, up from 54 the year before, in order to reach more people on social media. In response to the criticism, the US Open sent reminders to ticket holders and suite holders and displayed messages on video boards asking fans not to use flash photography or other lighting devices. The tournament also said that two influencers had been given credentials by mistake, and their access was removed.
Some experts believe that influencers will continue to be part of major sporting events, so the debate is unlikely to end soon.
